Redesign Has Pluses and Minuses - I ordered two of these to replace a couple of older ones because the lids cracked in half (see photo). I've had four or five of these lids break along the left side, up to the red disc. Happens every time after a few months of use. Anyway, I haven't had the new ones long enough to see if they too will break, but I'm not a fan of the redesign. The new design has a wire basket with a lid, like the old one, but the basket then goes inside a plastic shell with a single hole in the bottom. So preparing one for use requires two steps instead of one, and cleaning is a pain. The old basket had a "handle" that I used to rap on the edge of a bowl to shake the grounds loose (I save my grounds for gardening). The new basket lacks the handle and is generally sort of flimsy, making it difficult to empty.
Also, the new design allows you to make either a cup or a carafe. Okay, not a bad idea, except that now you have to go through another menu, in which you must select either a picture of a carafe or a number, 1-6; then you get to another screen where you can select the size. There's really no explanation of what the numbers mean (I know, it's probably in the Keurig manual somewhere) so we just guess and then see what we get.
The whole thing is annoying. Amazon is famous for reducing transactional friction; it's disappointing when a company goes out of its way to increase friction.
On the plus side, a cup of coffee seems to brew more quickly. Haven't actually timed the two models, but it feels faster.
Regarding Keurig customer service: I recently posted a question about the cracking lids, and someone from Keurig suggested that I call customer support. I did, and it was a waste of time. The rep took all my personal info down and said he would pass it on to someone else who might be able to do something about replacing the broken lids. Or not, he wasn't sure. That was the last I've heard from them.

Does not reduce Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) - You may find reviews discounting the importance of a TDS measurement talking about what it doesn't measure. Those miss the point. Ok, there might be some other bad stuff that might get removed that is not part of a TDS measurement. That's great. However, that doesn't change the fact that TDS is measuring OTHER CONTAMINANTS THAT STILL REMAIN.

The Environmental Protection Agency's (EPA's) National Secondary Drinking Water Regulations (NSDWRs) limit TDS to 500mg/L. This filter does not reduce TDS below this level.

From the Environmental Protection Agency's Website:

National Secondary Drinking Water Regulations (NSDWRs)
NSDWRs (or secondary standards) are non-enforceable guidelines regulating contaminants that may cause cosmetic effects (such as skin or tooth discoloration) or aesthetic effects (such as taste, odor, or color) in drinking water. EPA recommends secondary standards to water systems but does not require systems to comply with the standard. However, states may choose to adopt them as enforceable standards

List of National Secondary Drinking Water Regulations
Contaminant Secondary Standard
Aluminum 0.05 to 0.2 mg/L
Chloride 250 mg/L
Color 15 (color units)
Copper 1.0 mg/L
Corrosivity noncorrosive
Fluoride 2.0 mg/L
Foaming Agents 0.5 mg/L
Iron 0.3 mg/L
Manganese 0.05 mg/L
Odor 3 threshold odor number
pH 6.5-8.5

However, as you will see in one of the replies to this, the manufacturer claims it is built to the 53 standard but is in an extended process of certification.

So while the LG part costs more, you are getting a product that has been certified to perform better. I will opt for the LG for now, since one can never know what metals, benzene, and other contaminants may be in your local water supply, but you may make your own decision as to whether the manufacturer can be taken at their word. You can search google for the difference in standards, but here is a link: http://www.wqpmag.com/not-all-filters-are-created-or-tested-equal, where it explains 42 aims for taste and odor ONLY, and 53 aims for health-related claims.

As for how these actually make the water taste, I had no issues at all with that, and they worked properly for six months each, so for that reason along I might recommend them to those on a tight budget. I would guess that people with softer water can expect more longevity from these than those with hard water.

Glad This Came With TWO - Broke First One - One of the places my family goes a lot has a Keurig. We don't generally like most of the prepacks of coffee, so we like to take our own. The problem is that some of the containers are rejected, so I wanted one that wouldn't be. Well, glad this came with two.

WHAT ARE THESE LIKE?
This comes with a black and a purple version. The cap opens up and you put the coffee in. You put it in the Keurig and use it, and then normal use would cause it to work. In my case.. *sighs*

WATCH WHAT YOU ARE DOING!
My daughter grabbed the one container I had with me and ran off to make her coffee. She had it in a bag, poured it in and then proceeded to slam the container into the unit, not realizing that you have to put it in ONE DIRECTION ONLY. IF YOU DON'T DO THAT IT WILL POKE A HOLE IN THE UNIT. That is precisely what happened to ours.

DOES THE OTHER ONE WORK?
The other one works as long as the person using it lines up the correct direction BEFORE trying to use it. IT seemed to perform well and the machine did not reject it. So, now I only have one, which is why I wanted two- they could ruin one and mine would stay intact.

CLEAN UP
Clean up is good . I used a tiny scrub brush gently to get the mesh clean.

THE BOTTOM LINE
As long as you use this properly it should work with the machine. If you don't it will poke a hole in it. The coffee works out well if you use it right.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. I wish these had a more noticeable marking on it to keep this from being used incorrectly. But it is up to use to take our time to use it- as long as the family does not get a hold of it.
